decisions.reason: A flagship reference class electrometer is core to the firm's dosimetry business and has a long product life, so withdrawal within a year is very unlikely.
The risk management software supports the firm's strategy of integrated, predictive QA, though as a newer software category it carries somewhat more uncertainty.
A CT image quality phantom builds on the firm's established imaging QA offer and fits its flagship imaging QA line, so it will likely stay.
The mammography phantom is further from the core business but complements the newly expanded imaging QA portfolio, so it is likely kept in its second year.
The full field mammography phantom broadens imaging QA coverage, but it overlaps somewhat with Product D, so there is a modest risk of consolidation.
This flagship imaging QA instrument line marks a strategic expansion and is very unlikely to be withdrawn soon.
